title: Largest Number
description:
Given a list of non-negative integers `nums`, arrange them such that they form the largest number and return it as a string.

Since the result may be very large, return a string instead of an integer. The returned string must not contain unnecessary leading zeros (for example, if `nums` contains only zeros such as `[0, 0]`, return `"0"`).
hints: Standard lexicographical string comparison fails on pairs like "3" and "30": "30" > "3", yet "330" > "303".
Compare two stringified numbers a and b by comparing the concatenations (a + b) and (b + a): a should come before b if (a + b) > (b + a).
Handle the all-zeros edge case: after sorting, if the largest element is "0", the entire answer is simply "0".

examples.explanation: Arranging as "2" followed by "10" forms "210", which is greater than "102".
Ordering as ["9", "5", "34", "3", "30"] yields the largest possible number "9534330".
Multiple zeros collapse to a single "0" rather than "00".
